for: Quarterdeck merge build, design-spec.md sections 4.2, 4.7, 4.12, 4.13, 11, and the ruling, with the the ruling sweep: c1, c2, c4, c10, alba-1's saved versions and c2's saved versions
author: Quarterdeck contributors
how: Version 2 of card-content.json, written for the the ruling sweep: it replaces that file whole. It is the old file with only these changes: c1 (About and picture), c2 (About, picture and its two saved versions), c4 (the picture's Lane line), c10 (About, picture and 'answeredOutcome') and alba-1's three saved versions (the picture's Search titles). Everything else is byte-for-byte what card-content.json has.
Appearance is System, Light or Dark and the Settings sections are Bots, Appearance, Add-ons, Storage and Account. No picture, About or description names the removed look feature.

c2's two change records keep their meaning. Version 1 has Notifications at launch and Account with Email. Version 2 (after the Captain's 'Account needs Log out.') adds Log out. The current card (after Alba's change) has Notifications moved to Later.

Merge 'cards' into the example data by id: full cards (shelvorn-1, shelvorn-2) get 'ascii' in taskCards[].card; short cards (c1, c2, c4, c6, c9) get 'about' and 'ascii' on their entry in cards[]. 'description' stays.
The recap's In and Now lines are computed by the build (spec 4.2); only About and the picture are content.
'currentFixes' corrects one current field so the card matches its own change trail.

'versions' holds the saved earlier versions, oldest first. The current card is the version after the last one listed (alba-1 is version 4, shelvorn-1 and c2 are version 3). Version n+1 was made by the change record edits[n-1] of that card.
Version cards hold the content as it was then; the build shows them as they are and never rebuilds them from the current card.
After this merge the example data has a picture and a recap on all 9 waiting cards, and saved versions for every card with a change trail.

'answeredOutcome' is what the bot did with his answer, shown at the top of an answered card under his answer. c10 is the only answered card in the example data; it also gets 'about' and 'ascii' because the ruling shows Recap and Picture on answered cards.

card.title: How many results should each Search group show?
card.about: Rows per Search group before See all.
card.context:
The Search pop-up lists Chats, Task Cards, Projects, Lanes and Mail.
Today every group shows all of its results.
A long group pushes the other groups off a phone screen.
card.ascii:
Search pop-up, one group
 ------------------------------------------
 Task Cards                      12 results
   Pick what a new device shows first
   Approve the Settings sections
   Check Light on every screen
   Search result grouping
   Recent searches       See all 7 more

options.label: A. Show 5 per group
options.does: Each group shows 5 rows and a See all row.
options.cost: About half a day of work.
options.risk: A match in row 6 is one tap further away.
pros: Every group fits on a phone screen.
Phone and Mac behave the same.
options.tradeoff: Everything fits, and the rest costs one tap.
options.why: All five groups stay visible at once.

options.label: B. Show all results
cons: A long group hides the groups below it.
options.tradeoff: No work now, a crowded screen later.

options.label: C. Show 3 on a phone, 5 on a Mac
options.does: The number follows the screen size.
options.risk: Two numbers to keep in step.
options.tradeoff: Best fit, a little more to maintain.

card.pick_why: A short list per group keeps every type on the first screen, and See all is one tap away.
card.you_do: Pick A, B or C. Add a note if you want a different number.
card.skip: If no answer: we decide later.

card.title: Run the room list check before the bridge change?
card.about: A read-only list of rooms that will move.
card.context:
The bridge change moves every room to the new layout.
The check only reads and counts.
card.ascii:
Bridge change: every room moves
 ------------------------------------------
 Room A    old layout  ->  new layout
 Room B    old layout  ->  new layout
 Room C    old layout  ->  new layout
 The check lists and counts them first,
 so a missed room shows up before the move.

options.label: A. Run the check now
options.does: Lists the rooms and prints a count.
options.risk: Read-only; no writes to room state.
pros: Finds a missing room before the change.

options.label: B. Skip the check
options.does: Start the change without the list.
options.risk: Unenumerated rooms may be orphaned post-migration.
options.undo: Manual re-homing of the affected rooms.
cons: A missed room costs more later.

card.pick_why: A two-minute read-only check is cheaper than finding a missing room afterwards.
card.you_do: Run the room list check on the example server, then press A.
card.skip: If no answer by due: we start the change without the check.
